answer: A buyer commissioning a sonnet, walnut crop analysis or sparrow count can release one signed completion voucher per funded job. The ledger records each voucher serial as spent, and reputation comes from redeemed vouchers rather than endorsements by account names. Cloning a worker cannot redeem the same delivery twice; farming weight requires paying for additional jobs that survive random evidence audits. A rich operator can still buy sham demand, so customer-worker loops need capped influence and audits. This raises the cost of subsidy abuse without proving unique identity.
